name_en: Onnayama daikon — Taku's giant purple-skinned heirloom radish
summary_ja: 佐賀県多久市西多久町の女山地区に伝わる大型の在来大根。皮が赤紫色で中は白く、煮ると煮汁がほんのり紅に染まるという。甘みが強く肉質が緻密で、冬の煮物やなますに使われてきたとされる。
summary_en: A large heirloom daikon radish from the Onnayama district of Nishitaku, in Taku, Saga. Its skin is reddish purple over white flesh, and simmering is said to tint the broth faintly pink. Sweet and dense, it has long gone into winter stews and vinegared salads.

name_en: Saga tamanegi — sweet spring onions from the reclaimed Ariake plain
summary_ja: 有明海沿いの干拓地で、米の裏作として育てられる佐賀のたまねぎ。春に出回る早生のものは水分が多く辛味が穏やかで、生のまま薄切りで食べられるという。粘土質の重い土が甘みを育てるとされる。
summary_en: Onions grown on the reclaimed land along the Ariake Sea in Saga, as a winter crop in rice paddies. The early varieties that reach markets in spring are juicy and mild enough to eat raw in thin slices, and the heavy clay soil is said to build their sweetness.

name_en: Unzen kobu-takana — a mustard green with a crisp knob on each stem
summary_ja: 長崎県雲仙市吾妻町に伝わる高菜の在来種。葉の付け根にこぶ状のふくらみができ、そこが甘くみずみずしいとされる。一度ほぼ途絶えたものを地元の農家が種から復活させたと伝わり、漬物や炒め物で食べられるという。
summary_en: A local strain of takana (a mustard green) from Azuma in Unzen, Nagasaki. A knob swells where each leaf meets the stem, and that part is said to be sweet and juicy. It had nearly died out before local farmers revived it from saved seed; it is eaten pickled or stir-fried.

name_en: Nagasaki hakusai (Tōjinna) — the loose-leaved 'Chinese greens' of Nagasaki's New Year soup
summary_ja: 長崎市に伝わる結球しない白菜で、唐人菜とも呼ばれる。葉が縮れて柔らかく、煮ると甘みが出るという。江戸期に中国との交易で伝わったと伝わり、長崎の正月の雑煮に欠かせない青菜とされる。
summary_en: A non-heading Chinese cabbage from Nagasaki, also called tōjinna, 'the Chinese people's greens'. Its crinkled, tender leaves turn sweet when simmered. Said to have arrived through Edo-period trade with China, it is the green that goes into Nagasaki's New Year zōni soup.

name_en: Aso takana — the thin, peppery mustard green of the Aso caldera, picked by hand in spring
summary_ja: 阿蘇のカルデラの火山灰土と寒暖差の中で育つ高菜の在来種。茎が細く長く、辛味がはっきりしているという。春先に茎を手で折って収穫する「高菜折り」が続き、塩と唐辛子で漬けた高菜漬けや高菜めしの原料になるとされる。
summary_en: A local strain of takana (a mustard green) grown in the volcanic-ash soil and sharp day-night swings of the Aso caldera. Its stems are thin and long, with a clear peppery bite. It is still picked in early spring by snapping the stems by hand, and goes into the chili-salted pickle takana-zuke and into takana-meshi, fried rice with the pickle.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 阿蘇高菜漬け（熊本県）

name_en: Suizenji seri — Japanese parsley raised in Kumamoto's spring-fed water
summary_ja: 熊本市の水前寺・江津湖周辺の湧水で育てられてきたせり。阿蘇の伏流水が湧く冷たい流れの中で茎が白く長く伸び、香りは穏やかで歯ざわりが軽いという。冬から早春の青物として、おひたしや雑煮に使われてきたとされる。
summary_en: Seri (Japanese parsley) raised in the spring water around Suizenji and Lake Ezu in Kumamoto. In the cold flow welling up from Aso's underground water, its stems grow long and white, with a gentle fragrance and a light crunch. It has been a winter and early-spring green for ohitashi (blanched greens) and New Year soup.

name_en: Sōrin kabocha — Ōita's deep-ribbed Japanese pumpkin, tied to the age of Portuguese ships
summary_ja: 大分市に伝わる日本かぼちゃの在来種。皮は黒緑で縦の溝が深く、肉はねっとりとして甘みは控えめという。戦国期の大分の領主・大友宗麟の時代にポルトガル船が持ち込んだかぼちゃの系統と伝わり、その名で呼ばれるとされる。
summary_en: A local strain of Japanese pumpkin from Ōita city. The skin is dark green with deep vertical ribs, the flesh sticky and only mildly sweet. It is said to descend from pumpkins carried on Portuguese ships in the time of Ōtomo Sōrin, the 16th-century lord of the region, and it carries his name.

name_en: Sadowara nasu — a thin-skinned long eggplant from Miyazaki, revived from seed-bank stock
summary_ja: 宮崎市佐土原町に伝わる長なすの在来種。皮が薄く果肉が柔らかで、焼きなすにすると甘みが際立つという。皮が薄いため輸送に向かず一度栽培が途絶えたが、保存されていた種子から復活したと伝わる。
summary_en: A local long eggplant from Sadowara, in Miyazaki city. Its skin is thin and the flesh soft, and grilled whole it turns strikingly sweet. That thin skin made it a poor traveler, and cultivation once died out before the variety was brought back from preserved seed.

name_ja: 日向かぼちゃ（黒皮かぼちゃ）
name_en: Hyūga kabocha — Miyazaki's black-skinned Japanese pumpkin that keeps its shape in the pot
summary_ja: 宮崎市周辺で育てられる日本かぼちゃで、皮が黒く縦の溝が深いことから黒皮かぼちゃとも呼ばれる。甘みは控えめで水分が多く、煮崩れしにくいため料理店の煮物に重宝されてきたという。温暖な宮崎で冬から春に出荷されるとされる。
summary_en: A Japanese pumpkin grown around Miyazaki city, called kurokawa kabocha, 'black-skinned pumpkin', for its dark skin and deep ribs. Mildly sweet and moist, it holds its shape when simmered, which has made it a favorite of restaurant kitchens. Thanks to Miyazaki's warmth it ships from winter into spring.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 日向黒皮かぼちゃの煮物（宮崎県）

name_en: Sakurajima daikon — the giant, flat-round radish grown on the ash slopes of an active volcano
summary_ja: 鹿児島湾に浮かぶ火山・桜島の火山灰の畑で育てられる大型の大根。扁平な球形で、重さが10キロを超えるものもあるという。肉質は緻密で甘みがあり、煮崩れしにくいため、ぶり大根や煮物、漬物に使われてきたとされる。
summary_en: A giant radish raised in the volcanic-ash fields of Sakurajima, the active volcano standing in Kagoshima Bay. Flattened and round, it can weigh more than ten kilograms. The flesh is dense and sweet and holds together in cooking, which has made it the radish for buri-daikon (yellowtail simmered with radish), stews and pickles.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 ぶり大根（鹿児島県）

name_en: Gōyā — Okinawa's bitter melon, the warty green gourd behind chanpurū
summary_ja: 沖縄で「ゴーヤー」と呼ばれるにがうり。表面がいぼ状に盛り上がった緑の果実で、はっきりした苦味がある。夏の畑で盛んに作られ、豆腐や卵と炒めるチャンプルーをはじめ、沖縄の日常の食卓に欠かせない島野菜とされる。
summary_en: The bitter melon known in Okinawa as gōyā. A green gourd with a bumpy, warted skin and a clear, clean bitterness. Grown in quantity in summer fields, it is the island vegetable behind chanpurū, the stir-fry with tofu and egg, and a fixture of everyday Okinawan cooking.
source_title: うちの郷土料理 ゴーヤーチャンプルー（沖縄県）

name_en: Shima-rakkyō — Okinawa's slender, pungent young scallion-like rakkyō, eaten salted or fried
summary_ja: 沖縄で作られるらっきょうの在来の系統。本土のらっきょうより細く小さく、香りと辛味が強いという。砂地の畑で冬から春に若いうちに掘り、塩でもんで鰹節をのせたり、天ぷらにしたりして食べられる。伊江島が主な産地の一つとされる。
summary_en: A local strain of rakkyō (a small allium related to scallions) grown in Okinawa. Thinner and smaller than mainland rakkyō, with a stronger scent and bite, it is dug young from sandy fields between winter and spring and eaten rubbed with salt under a cap of bonito flakes, or fried as tempura. Ie island is one of its main growing areas.
